smells.finding: scripts/mcp_spine_server.py:call_tool() is ~130 lines dispatching all 7 tools by string name, each with its own if/elif sub-actions (spine_lease: claim/release/heartbeat; spine_evidence: attest/waive/attach; spine_halt: block/resume; spine_survey_result: record/consolidate). It is readable (each block is a short, self-contained argv builder) but a single function carrying the full tool surface is a candidate for splitting into one handler function per tool name, dispatched from a dict, which would also shrink call_tool's own cyclomatic complexity. Not a blocker -- it mirrors the flat TOOLS list structure it dispatches and every branch is a straightforward CLI-argv builder, not business logic.
No classes in mcp_spine_server.py or gen_mcp_config.py -- both are module-level function dispatch, appropriate for a stateless stdio server.

The repeated 'err = _require(args, ...); if err: return _tool_error(...)' shape across call_tool's branches is boilerplate already deduped through the shared _require/_tool_error helpers -- not literal duplication.

Every function operates on its own module-level state (ENGINE/SPINE/SESSION) and its own args dict; no function reaches into another module's internals beyond the single sanctioned call into checklist_engine.main().

task_id/condition_id/which travel together for attest/waive, but this is the JSON-RPC tool-args shape mirroring the CLI's own --cond/--which flags 1:1 -- not an ad hoc clump that should be a value object.

Action strings (claim/release/heartbeat, attest/attach/waive, block/resume, record/consolidate) are raw strings in Python, but each tool's inputSchema already declares them as a JSON Schema enum -- the structure lives at the correct boundary (the MCP tool contract), not missing.

gen_mcp_config.py:build_config() takes 7 params, but only 3 (spine_file, session_id, agent_id) are required -- engine/server/server_name/python all default to the repo's own vendored paths / sys.executable. Each param maps 1:1 to a CLI flag in parse_args(), which is the function's entire purpose (compose the --mcp-config JSON from named CLI inputs).
This is a new, additive module; no existing call site had to change in more than one place to accommodate it (checklist_engine.py diff is empty).
New files with no change history yet -- divergent change is a property of a file's edit history over time, not observable on a first commit.
No a.b().c().d() chains; run_engine()->as_result() is a two-step pipeline, not a chain walking through several objects' internals.

gen_mcp_config.py's --python/--server-name override knobs look like unused generality at first glance, but CREW_CONTEXT.md's own Python-Invocation section documents that 'python' and 'py' resolve to materially different interpreters on this host family -- making the interpreter overridable is a direct, documented response to a real doctrine concern, not speculative.

The module docstrings are long but explain WHY (the tool-grouping decision, the CLI-fallback rationale, the delivery-path measurement) -- durable design record matching this repo's decision-anchor doctrine, not a bad-code cover-up. The code itself does not rely on the comments to be understood.
